newsitem.title: USA: CSCE dairy options plan 'promising' - USDA official.
newsitem.headline: CSCE dairy options plan 'promising' - USDA official.

text.p: A proposal by the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange for a pilot options program involving dairy farmers was "very promising" but questions of cost remained, a U.S. Agriculture Department official said Tuesday.
"The budget neutrality question is one that we are examining," said Ken Ackerman, head of USDA's Risk Management Agency.

In response to questions by Senator Herb Kohl, Wisconsin Democrat, at a Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing, Ackerman said the CSCE proposal was viewed as "a very promising proposal...We are looking at it very actively."
Kohl raised the issue, saying an options program would be a way for dairy farmers to stablize income in the face of the loss at the end of 1999 of federal price supports.
The 1996 "Freedom to Farm" law allows USDA to offer pilot programs in which farmers buy and sell options contracts in lieu of receiving farm subsidies. USDA helps cover cost of the contracts.
Kohl said the dairy options program proposed by the CSCE, based in New York, might cost $10 million.
"I'd like to hope...that we in fact get something off the ground," he said.
